$comment: Written reasons for the capabilities catalogue (docs/DSL_CAPABILITIES.html), batch 1 of N, 2026-11-22 (owner: do only 20% of the remaining REG-357 cases, of mixed complexity). One reason per keyword: what need it serves and why a lower rung of the extension ladder (expression, function, flow step, hand-written code) or an existing keyword cannot do it. Evidence stays honest: where no official sample, or only the coverage fixture, uses the keyword, the reason says so. The batch is every 5th keyword, taken within each kind of value (boolean, text, number, choice, list, object, reference) so simple and complex ones are mixed. A keyword with a reason here no longer shows 'no written justification'. Key = slot id exactly as the catalogue shows it; the generator refuses a reason for a keyword the schema does not have.

reasons.actionMetadata.visibleWhen: A button that makes no sense for the current row, such as cancelling a shipped order, must disappear; a per-row condition on the action's presentation does that without a flow or hand-written UI code.
reasons.agentAccess.photoIntake: Chat bots receive photos, and turning one into a record needs the upload, the target box and an optional pre-fill procedure; without a declared mapping each app would hand-write the bot's intake.
reasons.agentAccessExposure.operations: An agent should be offered read-only tools by default and writes only when named; a closed list of operations per exposure is the narrowest way to say that, and permissions still check every call.
reasons.aggregateBalance.collection: A balance rule has to name which collection of the aggregate it partitions, including nested ones; a path into the composition tree is the only way to say it without code. Only the coverage fixture uses it.
reasons.aggregateBalance.quantityField: A balance rule sums one numeric box per side and group and must be told which one; it runs inside the commit, so no expression can pick it. Only the coverage fixture uses it, and no test names it.
reasons.aggregateCollection.orderBy: The children of an aggregate, such as invoice lines, must come back in a meaningful order every time; declaring it once on the collection stops each screen and agent from re-sorting.
reasons.aggregateFunction.field: An aggregate column needs the box it reads, except for count; declaring it keeps the query declarative and checkable, which a free expression would not be.
reasons.aggregateFunction.fn: A closed list of five aggregates lets the generated query be checked and pushed down to every supported database; an open expression could not be translated to SQL.
reasons.appShellNavItem.group: A back-office menu with dozens of entries needs section headings; a group label clusters entries without shell code and matches the shell's own grouping.
reasons.autoPanel.name: Generated back-office panels need a stable handle that other pieces point at; it defaults to one derived from the concept, so it is declared only to override. No official sample sets it.
reasons.autoPanel.prompt: A generated panel offers a row picker to its other pages, and its settings must be tunable in the same place; a nested surface block does that without hand-written pickers. No official sample sets it.
reasons.autoPanel.surfaces: Not every concept needs all four generated pages; listing the surfaces avoids generating and maintaining pages nobody opens, with a sensible default per kind of panel.
reasons.autoPanelSurface.filters: Back-office users need to narrow a long list by a few boxes; naming them keeps the generated list declarative, where an expression per column would be heavier to author.
reasons.autoPanelSurface.regions: A workbench region may be generated, hand-made or drawn as a cell grid, and is addressed by the aggregate's own tree; without a keyword every app would fork the workbench page.
reasons.awaitMatch.correlation: Many flow instances wait for the same kind of event and each must wake only for its own; a correlation flag does that without a match expression in every flow.
reasons.capability.http: An HTTP connector needs its address, login and timeouts; declared settings can be checked and keep secrets in the environment, where a flow step or code would scatter them.
reasons.capability.name: Flow steps and webhook triggers refer to an outside ability by a stable handle; a name unique in the model, pack-qualified when composed, is the minimum needed to wire them.
reasons.capabilityOperation.name: A flow call must say which operation of the capability it uses; the operation's own name is that handle, and policies, errors and authorization attach to it.
reasons.capabilityPolicy.circuitOpenMs: A circuit breaker without a cool-down would stay open forever or retry at once; this value says how long to rest before a trial call. Only the coverage fixture uses it.
reasons.capabilityPolicy.failureClassification: Retrying only makes sense for transient failures; a default classification per call, overridable per error, lets resilience be declared instead of coded. Only the coverage fixture uses it.
reasons.cellGrid.colsField: Boards differ in width from record to record, so the column count has to come from data and not from the model; naming the box that holds it keeps the board generated.
reasons.cellGrid.defaultRows: A board needs a size even when no record states one; a default row count gives a safe starting grid.
reasons.concept.collaboration: Comment threads and mentions on records are common, and hand-written code would repeat them for every concept; a declarative switch generates the thread, its storage and its permissions.
reasons.concept.fields: A concept is its fields; this list, at least one and in display order, is the core vocabulary from which forms, tables and APIs are generated.
reasons.concept.name: Everything refers to a concept by one name: its table, its REST resource and every reference; a unique PascalCase name is the minimum identity the generator needs.
reasons.concept.truthLevel: The release gate must refuse to promote a concept whose behavior was never verified; a declared maturity level from T0 to T6 lets the gate compare the claim with the evidence.
reasons.conceptAccess.write: Who may change or delete a row depends on the row itself, such as its owner; a per-record expression keeps the rule in the model and enforced by the platform instead of scattered checks.
reasons.context.$ref: A bounded context lives in its own fragment file so teams can work apart; the reference is how composition finds that file, by the same mechanism as fragments and packs.
reasons.conversion.into: Splitting one stored box into several, such as a full name into first and last, must say which target gets which part; a list of target boxes with a rule each states it. Only the coverage fixture uses it.
reasons.conversion.to: Every conversion writes its result somewhere; naming the target box lets the compiler check that it exists and derive which boxes the hook touches. Only the coverage fixture uses it.
reasons.conversionLookupMatch.equals: A lookup conversion must say which box of the converted concept is compared with the other concept's box; it is one half of the join. Only the coverage fixture uses it.
reasons.documentBand.label: A printed band needs a heading such as Items; a localizable label keeps it in the model, so documents print in the reader's language.
reasons.documentColumn.field: A report column must say which box of the concept it prints, so that field access can omit what the viewer may not read. Only the coverage fixture uses it.
reasons.documentColumn.total: Reports end groups with subtotals and a grand total, and each column needs its own calculation; a closed list of aggregates states it, computed on readable rows only. Only the coverage fixture uses it.
reasons.enumOption.badge: A status shown as a coloured chip next to its label is easier to scan than plain text; a short badge text or colour token per option keeps that presentation in the model.
reasons.enumOption.default: New records should start with the usual choice preselected; marking one option as the default covers the simplest case without a default expression.
reasons.event.name: Flows publish, trigger on and await events by name, so each event needs one unique name; it is the contract between parts of an app that never call each other.
reasons.event.payload: Receivers of an event need to know what it carries; a list of named, optionally typed fields is the minimal contract, and it lets mappings and handlers be checked.
reasons.field.connectable: A natural key such as a tax number can be what other concepts reference instead of a generated id; marking a unique box as an anchor makes that reference legal and keeps the foreign key stable.
reasons.field.derivedExpression: A total should never be typed; a formula over the row's other boxes, computed by the platform and refused from clients, keeps it consistent where a default expression would only fill it once.
reasons.field.file: A file box stores a handle, never raw bytes, and needs limits on type and size; a metadata block keeps those rules enforced by the platform instead of by each client.
reasons.field.min: A quantity must not be negative; an inclusive lower bound on numeric boxes is enforced on every write and shown in generated forms, which an invariant would check only after the fact.
reasons.field.renamedFrom: Renaming a column must not look like dropping one and adding another, which loses data; naming the old column lets the schema lifecycle classify it as a rename. Only the coverage fixture uses it.
reasons.field.ui: Presentation hints such as label, placeholder and grouping belong with the box but are not data rules; one block of hints keeps the generated UI declarative without a new keyword per hint.
reasons.field.uniqueItems: An array box such as a list of tags must not repeat an element; a flag on the box states it once, where an invariant would need a custom expression. Only the coverage fixture uses it, and no test names it.
reasons.flow.hooks: A shop wants to add one step to a pack's standard flow without copying all of it; hooks insert steps before or after a named step. Only the coverage fixture uses it.
reasons.flow.specializes: Reusing a pack's flow and changing a little is better than forking it; naming the base flow lets the new one add hooks only. Only the coverage fixture uses it, and no test names it.
reasons.flowHook.position: An inserted step is only meaningful relative to its target; before or after is the whole choice. Only the coverage fixture uses it.
reasons.flowStep.action: Traces and action histories should show a readable label and a danger level for a step, not an internal name; presentation metadata keeps that out of the step's logic.
reasons.flowStep.awaitEvent: A durable flow must be able to stop until something happens; naming the awaited event is what makes the wait resumable across restarts, which a loop in code could not survive.
reasons.flowStep.dedupeKey: A scheduled reminder must not be created again each time the flow runs; a dedupe key makes the schedule unique across executions. Only the coverage fixture uses it, and no test names it.
reasons.flowStep.delaySeconds: Reminders and follow-ups happen later; a delay in seconds on a scheduling step is the simplest durable way, without a cron expression or a polling loop.
reasons.flowStep.id: Reading or deleting one record needs its id; a reference to it is the narrowest input a concept step needs.
reasons.flowStep.invariants: Rules already declared on a concept should be re-checked inside a flow without being rewritten; listing their names reuses them, so the flow cannot drift from the concept.
reasons.flowStep.message: A notification needs a body, either fixed text or built from the flow's data; one keyword covers both without a separate formatting step.
reasons.flowStep.output: Later steps need earlier results; naming the state key that holds a step's output is how a flow passes data between steps without shared variables.
reasons.flowStep.select: Shaping a small object from a bigger record, or one per list item, is common in flows; declaring the fields once replaces a hand-written mapping step.
reasons.flowStep.type: A flow is made of different kinds of step, from checks to waits to concept work; a closed list of types lets each be validated, executed and shown in traces.
reasons.guidePage.gadgets: A start page is a set of tiles, charts and lists; declaring them as a list keeps the page generated and rearrangeable without writing a page by hand.
reasons.guidePage.theme: A start page may need its own accent, density and logo, separate from the app theme; a theme block keeps those few visual settings declarative.
reasons.guidePageGadget.name: Gadgets on one page must be told apart for ordering and references; a name unique on the page is enough.
reasons.guidePageGadget.y: A chart or number tile must know which query column carries the value; naming it keeps gadgets declarative over a query.
reasons.guidePageRegion.collapsible: Side columns take room people sometimes need; letting users fold a region is a small usability setting that would otherwise need custom UI code.
reasons.guidePageTheme.mode: People work in bright or dim places; a mode setting lets a start page choose its colour mode without a separate stylesheet.
reasons.httpConnector.timeoutMs: A slow remote service must not hang a flow; a per-attempt deadline, with a safe default, makes failures bounded and classifiable.
reasons.httpConnectorOperation.method: A remote operation reads, creates, replaces or removes; the HTTP verb is part of the contract with the remote API and cannot be derived from anything else.
reasons.humanTask.assignee: A task for a person must say who may complete it, a named user, roles or both; the inbox and the permission check are built from this.
reasons.humanTask.description: A title alone rarely tells an approver what to decide; a longer description is shown with the task in the inbox.
reasons.inboundDoor.hmacSecretEnvVar: An open webhook must verify who is calling, using a shared secret that must never live in the model; naming the environment variable keeps the secret out of version control. Only the coverage fixture uses it, and no test names it.
reasons.inboundDoor.path: A third party posts to one fixed address; the path segment names it, defaults to the capability's name and is required for pack capabilities so it never changes. No official sample sets it.
reasons.invariant.fields: Uniqueness across several boxes together, such as branch plus number, cannot be a per-box flag; listing the fields states a compound unique rule that the database can enforce.
reasons.invariant.override: A specializing concept sometimes needs to replace an inherited rule instead of adding a second one; the flag says so explicitly rather than by a silent name clash.
reasons.invariant.specializes: A concept that refines an inherited rule should name it, so the relation is checked and documented instead of guessed.
reasons.lifecycleTransition.action: A state-change button needs a confirmation text, a success message and a danger level; metadata on the transition keeps them out of the guard logic.
reasons.lifecycleTransition.guard: Whether a transition is allowed depends on the row, for example only when all lines are priced; a guard expression over the row keeps the lifecycle honest without a flow.
reasons.lifecycleTransition.metadata: Authors sometimes need to note why a transition exists; free-form string notes ride along in the compiled model without affecting behavior.
reasons.pack:capabilities: A pack for payments or mail brings the outside abilities it needs; contributing capabilities lets consumers use it without declaring them again.
reasons.pack:extensionPoints: A pack keeps most members private but may allow a few to be specialized; extension points name them without making them public. No official sample uses it yet.
reasons.pack:migrations: A pack's version history needs a replay chain so apps can upgrade across releases; the publish command fills it, so it is a subsystem output more than a hand-authored keyword.
reasons.pack:namespace: Generated code for a pack needs a package home; an optional namespace lets an author choose it instead of a derived default.
reasons.pack:private: A pack has helpers that must stay internal; listing private names makes outside references fail at composition. No official sample uses it yet.
reasons.pack:seeds: A pack may ship first-boot rows such as a list of countries; declaring seeds in the pack keeps them versioned with the concepts they fill. No official sample uses it yet.
reasons.pack:version: Apps pin and upgrade packs by version; a required major, minor and patch number is the minimum for compatibility checks.
reasons.panelAction.filename: A downloaded file should get a meaningful name; the filename is required with download results because the browser needs it.
reasons.panelAction.resultAs: An export button should hand over a real file, not a page of JSON; the download setting on a procedure action does that, with a filename and a content type.
reasons.panelDataSource.childField: A nested list such as order lines must know which of its boxes points at the parent; the child field is half of that link.
reasons.panelDataSource.params: A panel's query or procedure needs its blanks filled from the page; params bind them with literals or expressions. No official sample sets it.
reasons.panelDataSource.parentField: The other half of the master-detail link is the parent box the child points to; naming it lets the nested list be generated.
reasons.panelDataSource.rowOps: A nested list may allow adding lines, deleting them or both; a closed list states which, and the panel enforces it.
reasons.panelFieldBinding.field: A panel binds boxes of its data sources one by one; each binding must name the box it is about.
reasons.panelWidget.chart: A chart's categories can be drawn as bars, a line or a doughnut; a closed choice lets the generated panel render each consistently.
reasons.panelWidget.dataSource: A tile, chart or table needs rows from one of the panel's lists; naming it ties the widget to its data.
reasons.presentationMetadata.customWidgetRef: When no ready-made control fits, such as a signature pad, a custom widget supplied with the app can render the box; a path to it is the escape hatch. No official sample uses it yet.
reasons.presentationMetadata.deprecated: A box kept for old data must stay stored but be hidden from new entries; a flag says so without deleting the column. No official sample uses it yet.
reasons.presentationMetadata.enabledWhen: A box such as discount reason should be editable only while a condition holds; an expression over the record in the presentation block avoids a flow. No official sample uses it yet.
reasons.presentationMetadata.listColumnOrder: Lists read best with the important column first; a position per box orders list columns without reordering the concept. No official sample uses it yet.
reasons.presentationMetadata.requiredWhen: A box required only in some situations, such as a cancel reason on a cancelled order, needs a conditional rule that is marked and enforced; a plain required flag cannot say it. No official sample uses it yet.
reasons.presentationMetadata.searchFields: A picker for a reference should search by the boxes people remember, such as name and tax number; listing them avoids a custom search. No official sample uses it yet.
reasons.presentationMetadata.shortLabel: Table headers and mobile cards have little room; a short label per box keeps the full label for forms.
reasons.presentationMetadata.summaryCard: A record's summary card shows only the few boxes that matter; a flag per box chooses them without a layout. No official sample uses it yet.
reasons.presentationMetadata.width: Some controls need a narrower or wider column; a preferred width states it as a CSS size or a keyword. No official sample uses it yet.
reasons.property.default: A setting must have a value even when no scope sets one; the least specific level of the cascade is the property's own default, checked against its type.
reasons.query.having: After grouping and computing columns, a report often keeps only some groups; having filters the grouped output, which a where clause cannot do because it runs before grouping.
reasons.query.lookups: A grouped query sometimes needs a total from another concept beside each row, such as stock beside needs; lookups merge per-key aggregates without a second query or code.
reasons.queryLookup.concept: A lookup adds up the rows of another concept and has to say which one.
reasons.queryParameter.description: People calling a query need to know what each blank means; a sentence per parameter documents it for humans and for AI authors.
reasons.referenceDefinition.displayTemplate: A picked reference should read code and name together, not as an id; a template over the target's boxes states it once.
reasons.referenceDefinition.inlineCreate: Sometimes the user should create the missing target from inside the picker, and sometimes not; allow or deny states it per reference.
reasons.referenceDefinition.previewFields: Hovering over a reference should reveal a few facts about the target; listing the boxes keeps the preview generated.
reasons.role.concepts: Permissions per concept and operation are the heart of access control; mapping concept names to allowed operations is declarative, checked at validation and enforced at boot and on each call.
reasons.role.name: Experiences, access rules and capability rules refer to a role by name; a unique name is the minimum identity.
reasons.root:conversions: Changing the schema must carry stored data along; declarative conversions run at boot and are checked at compile time, which hand-written SQL scripts would not be. Only the coverage fixture uses it.
reasons.root:externalAi: Delegating work to an outside AI must be an explicit opt-in with named vendors, prompts and limits; one block keeps that governance in the model.
reasons.root:flows: What the app does over time, including waiting and compensation, is a durable list of steps; flows are the behavior layer of the model and are what triggers start.
reasons.root:propertyScopes: The cascade of settings needs its levels declared, most specific first; their order is the resolution order.
reasons.root:sequences: Documents such as invoices need numbers that are never repeated per scope; a declared counter with a format lets a default expression allocate the next number atomically.
reasons.schemaObject.derivedExpression: A structured value sometimes has a part computed from its siblings; the same derived-expression idea as for fields works inside objects. No official sample uses it yet.
reasons.schemaObject.maxLength: A text inside a structured value needs a length limit just like a field; the same keyword keeps the rule consistent.
reasons.schemaObject.scale: A decimal inside a structured value needs a number of digits after the point; scale states it. No official sample uses it yet.
reasons.seed.id: A starting row sometimes must have a known id so that others refer to it; an explicit id overrides the generated UUID. Only the coverage fixture uses it.
reasons.seed.repeatOver: Bulk starting data such as a grid of seats is a product of ranges; repeat over generates one row per combination instead of writing each out. Only the coverage fixture uses it.
reasons.sequence.name: A default expression asks for the next number by name; the name is deliberately not pack-qualified so counters stay stable across composition.
reasons.sequence.scope: Some counters are shared by everyone and some must run per customer account; the scope says which.
reasons.transactionHooks.onCommit: Something must happen right after a save, such as a message; naming a procedure or flow runs it after the commit. No official sample uses it yet.
reasons.workbenchAction.afterAction: After a helper procedure runs, the draft has to take in its result in ways no fixed rule covers; an after-action procedure returning a patched draft is the general form. Only the coverage fixture uses it.
reasons.workbenchAction.inputFields: Some workbench actions need a value from the person before running, such as a quantity; listing the inputs makes NPDev ask for them.
reasons.workbenchAction.label: A button should say what it does in the user's words; the label defaults to the procedure's name when omitted.
reasons.workbenchAction.review: When a helper proposes many changes the person should accept only some; review shows them field by field and folds in only the ticked ones, with nothing saved until Save.
reasons.workbenchBandPicker.panel: The workbench's row picker needs a list to show; naming a selection panel reuses an existing one. Only the coverage fixture uses it.
